summary: Reviewed all 65 occurrences. Null sense in a one-sense box does not make the embedded second III meaning disappear. Preserve the original English wording of recovered III.2 rather than silently translating it.

I noquṣo/noquṣto/noquṣe and nuquṣto describe deficient states, including dowry, share, jug and water, but may be lexical adjectives. Their readings are useful evidence; they do not securely establish a productive I Part act. box.

Numeral noqəṣ functions as minus in arithmetic and clock-time expressions. Several contexts lack a finite event subject; retain the formula in Idiomatic phrases, with word-class question. The comparative measure in 94/380 is similarly held apart from a new finite-verb sense.

The inherited Detransitive Part. Pass. at 74/36 is already quoted; keep its Detransitive filing and unnumbered D1 convention, normalized to final sense 1 in the audit, until editors harmonize numbering. It does not prove every noncausative III form is Detransitive.
Glossary searches for noqəṣ, noquṣ and manqəṣ ruḥ were consulted before adding the numerical formula and submission construction. Existing lexical forms do not settle verbal derivation.
Are noquṣo/noquṣto/noquṣe/nuquṣto productive I Part act. forms, or independent adjectives? No new I Part act. box is published before this is settled (JTM 1.3/21; 96/146; 102/22; 115/134,138).
Is noqəṣ in numeral/time phrases and the 94/380 measurement a finite Infectum, a comparative adjective, or a lexical minus operator? The formula is recorded without a verbal paradigm claim.
Confirm ko-manqaṣle as ko-Preterit with l-series subject in MAC NE Mem and Zin/19; its repetition beside ko-manqaṣ supports that analysis.
Confirm naqəṣ no in 99/54 as separated qaṭəl person ending versus a loan adjective plus copula. Also check masculine noqəṣ beside feminine zaydo with price in 103/3.
Should the inherited Detransitive result-state sense at 74/36 receive its own Detransitive sense label 1, distinct from active III.2? Preserve the current reference pending editorial decision.
PrS 39/9 translates only the goose being taken, omitting Bnanne, naqiṣi. Do not quote an invented shortage translation.
Correct Sehrkraft to Sehkraft.
rationale: The German word is Sehkraft. The supplied edition translation at 3/22 has Sehkraft abnimmt.
